name: Chapter 5: Continuity and Differentiability
description: Continuity, algebra of continuous functions, differentiability, chain rule, implicit, inverse trig, exponential and logarithmic differentiation, parametric forms, second derivatives, and exam-style problems.

cards.term: Definition of continuity of f at x = c.
cards.definition: f is continuous at c if lim x→c f(x) = f(c). That means the left limit, the right limit and f(c) all exist and are equal

cards.term: What three things must hold for continuity at c?
cards.definition:
(1) f(c) is defined; (2) lim x→c f(x) exists (left limit = right limit); (3) the limit equals f(c).
Breaking any one gives a point of discontinuity

cards.term: Three types of discontinuity
cards.definition: Continuous at c iff left limit = right limit = f(c); removable (limit exists, differs from f(c)), jump (one-sided limits differ), infinite (no limit)

cards.term: What does “f is continuous” mean for a function on an interval [a, b]?
cards.definition: Continuous at every interior point, right-continuous at a (lim x→a⁺ f(x) = f(a)) and left-continuous at b (lim x→b⁻ f(x) = f(b))

cards.term: Pen test for continuity?
cards.definition: Can you draw the graph around the point without lifting the pen? A jump, hole, or blow-up forces you to lift it. (A function like 1/x is continuous on its domain, though its graph has a gap at 0 where it is not defined)

cards.term: Example 1: continuity of f(x) = 2x + 3 at x = 1?
cards.definition: lim x→1 (2x + 3) = 5 = f(1): continuous

cards.term: Example 3: is f(x) = |x| continuous at 0? Everywhere?
cards.definition: Left limit lim(−x) = 0, right limit 0, f(0) = 0: continuous at 0. It is continuous at every real number (Example 7)

cards.term: Example 4: f(x) = x³ + 3 (x ≠ 0), f(0) = 1. Continuous at 0?
cards.definition: lim x→0 f(x) = 3 but f(0) = 1: not continuous. A removable discontinuity (fix f(0) = 3)

cards.term: Example 5 and 6: which constant functions and the identity function are continuous?
cards.definition: All of them, at every real number: lim x→c k = k and lim x→c x = c

cards.term: Example 10: f(x) = x + 2 (x ≤ 1), x − 2 (x > 1). Points of discontinuity?
cards.definition: At x = 1: left limit 3, right limit −1, differ. So x = 1 is the only point of discontinuity (a jump)

cards.term: Example 12: f(x) = x + 2 (x < 0), −x + 2 (x > 0). Continuous?
cards.definition: f is not defined at 0, so 0 is not in the domain; f is continuous at every point of its domain. Yes, continuous

cards.term: Example 13: f(x) = x² (x < 0), x (x ≥ 0). Continuous?
cards.definition: At 0: left limit 0, right limit 0, f(0) = 0. Elsewhere f is a polynomial: continuous everywhere

cards.term: Example 15: greatest integer function [x]. Where is it discontinuous?
cards.definition: At every integer c: left limit c − 1, right limit c (a jump of 1). Continuous at all non-integers

cards.term: Which functions are continuous everywhere on their domains?
cards.definition: Polynomials, rational functions (except where the denominator is 0), |x|, sin x, cos x, tan x (tan on its domain), exponentials, logarithms (x > 0), inverse trig on their domains

cards.term: Theorem 1: algebra of continuous functions.
cards.definition: If f, g are continuous at c: f + g, f − g, f·g, λf are continuous at c, and f/g too provided g(c) ≠ 0

cards.term: Theorem 2: continuity of a composite function.
cards.definition: If g is continuous at c and f is continuous at g(c), then f∘g is continuous at c. Example 19: sin(x²) is continuous; Example 20: |1 − x + |x|| is continuous

cards.term: Example 17: how is the continuity of sin x proved?
cards.definition: x = c + h, so lim x→c sin x = lim h→0 [sin c cos h + cos c sin h] = sin c · 1 + cos c · 0 = sin c, using cos h → 1 and sin h → 0

cards.term: Ex 5.1 Q1: prove f(x) = 5x − 3 is continuous at x = 0, −3 and 5.
cards.definition: A polynomial: lim x→c (5x − 3) = 5c − 3 = f(c) for c = 0, −3, 5. ✓ (values −3, −18, 22)

cards.term: Ex 5.1 Q2: continuity of f(x) = 2x² − 1 at x = 3.
cards.definition: lim x→3 (2x² − 1) = 17 = f(3): continuous

cards.term:
Ex 5.1 Q3: which of these are continuous?
(a) x − 5
(b) 1/(x − 5), x ≠ 5
(c) (x² − 25)/(x + 5), x ≠ −5
(d) |x − 5|
cards.definition: All four are continuous on their domains: (a) polynomial (b) rational (c) equals x − 5 wherever defined (d) composition of |x| and x − 5. (b) and (c) simply have no point at 5 and −5 in the domain

cards.term: Ex 5.1 Q4: prove f(x) = xⁿ (n a positive integer) is continuous at x = n.
cards.definition: lim x→n xⁿ = nⁿ = f(n) (a polynomial, or product of n continuous functions x). ✓

cards.term: Ex 5.1 Q5: f(x) = x (x ≤ 1), 5 (x > 1). Continuous at 0? at 1? at 2?
cards.definition: At 0: f = x near 0, continuous. At 1: left limit 1, right limit 5: not continuous. At 2: f = 5 near 2: continuous

cards.term: Ex 5.1 Q6: f(x) = 2x + 3 (x ≤ 2), 2x − 3 (x > 2). Points of discontinuity?
cards.definition: At 2: left limit 7, right limit 1. Discontinuous at x = 2

cards.term: Ex 5.1 Q7: f(x) = |x| + 3 (x ≤ −3), −2x (−3 < x < 3), 6x + 2 (x ≥ 3). Points of discontinuity?
cards.definition: At −3: left 6, right 6, f = 6: continuous. At 3: left −6, right 20: discontinuous at x = 3
For x > 0, f = 1; for x < 0, f = −1: left limit −1, right limit 1. Discontinuous at x = 0
For x < 0, x/|x| = −1. So f = −1 everywhere: no point of discontinuity
At 1: left limit 2, right limit 2, f(1) = 2: no point of discontinuity
At 2: left limit 5, right limit 5, f(2) = 5: no point of discontinuity
At 1: left limit 0, right limit 1: discontinuous at x = 1

cards.term: Ex 5.1 Q13: f(x) = x + 5 (x ≤ 1), x − 5 (x > 1). Continuous?
cards.definition: At 1: left limit 6, right limit −4: not continuous at x = 1
Jumps at x = 1 (3 → 4) and x = 3 (4 → 5): discontinuous at x = 1 and x = 3
At 0: left limit 0, f = 0: continuous. At 1: left value 0, right limit 4: x = 1 is the only point of discontinuity
At −1: left −2, right −2 ✓. At 1: left 2, right 2 ✓. Continuous everywhere

cards.term: Ex 5.1 Q17: f(x) = ax + 1 (x ≤ 3), bx + 3 (x > 3). Find the relation between a and b for continuity at 3.
cards.definition: 3a + 1 = 3b + 3 → 3a − 3b = 2 → a = b + 2/3

cards.term: Ex 5.1 Q18: f(x) = λ(x² − 2x) (x ≤ 0), 4x + 1 (x > 0). Continuity at 0 and at 1?
cards.definition: At 0: left limit 0, right limit 1. No value of λ makes it continuous at 0. At 1: f = 4x + 1 nearby, continuous for any λ

cards.term: Fractional part function x − [x] is discontinuous at integers
cards.definition: g(x) = x - [x] has left limit 1 and right limit 0 at each integer: discontinuous at all integers, continuous elsewhere; period 1 sawtooth

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Ex 5.1 Q19 · g(x) = x − [x]

Sketch g(x) = x − [x] (the fractional part). Where is it continuous?

Work out g on [0, 1), then repeat.

cards.term: Ex 5.1 Q20: is f(x) = x² − sin x + 5 continuous at x = π?
cards.definition: A sum of continuous functions: yes. lim x→π f = π² − 0 + 5 = f(π)

cards.term:
Ex 5.1 Q21: continuity of
(a) sin x + cos x
(b) sin x − cos x
(c) sin x · cos x.
cards.definition: Sums, differences and products of the continuous functions sin and cos: all continuous everywhere

cards.term: Ex 5.1 Q22: discuss the continuity of cos x, cosec x, sec x, cot x.
cards.definition: cos x continuous for all x. cosec x and cot x continuous except x = nπ. sec x continuous except x = (2n + 1)π/2 (n ∈ Z)

cards.term: Ex 5.1 Q23: f(x) = sin x/x (x < 0), x + 1 (x ≥ 0). Points of discontinuity?
cards.definition: At 0: left limit lim sin x/x = 1, f(0) = 1, right limit 1. No point of discontinuity

cards.term: Ex 5.1 Q24: f(x) = x² sin(1/x) (x ≠ 0), 0 (x = 0). Continuous?
cards.definition: Squeeze: |x² sin(1/x)| ≤ x² → 0 = f(0). Continuous for all x

cards.term: Ex 5.1 Q25: f(x) = sin x − cos x (x ≠ 0), −1 (x = 0). Continuous?
cards.definition: lim x→0 (sin x − cos x) = −1 = f(0): continuous for all x

cards.term: Ex 5.1 Q26: find k so that f(x) = k cos x/(π − 2x) (x ≠ π/2), 3 (x = π/2) is continuous at π/2.
cards.definition: Put x = π/2 + h: cos x = −sin h and π − 2x = −2h, so the limit is k/2. Set k/2 = 3: k = 6

cards.term: Ex 5.1 Q27: find k so that f = kx² (x ≤ 2), 3 (x > 2) is continuous at 2.
cards.definition: 4k = 3 → k = 3/4

cards.term: Ex 5.1 Q28: find k so that f = kx + 1 (x ≤ π), cos x (x > π) is continuous at π.
cards.definition: kπ + 1 = cos π = −1 → k = −2/π

cards.term: Ex 5.1 Q29: find k so that f = kx + 1 (x ≤ 5), 3x − 5 (x > 5) is continuous at 5.
cards.definition: 5k + 1 = 10 → k = 9/5

cards.term: Ex 5.1 Q30: find a, b so that f = 5 (x ≤ 2), ax + b (2 < x < 10), 21 (x ≥ 10) is continuous.
cards.definition: At 2: 2a + b = 5. At 10: 10a + b = 21. Subtract: 8a = 16: a = 2, b = 1

cards.term: Ex 5.1 Q31–33: show cos(x²), |cos x|, |sin x| are continuous.
cards.definition: Each is a composite of continuous functions (cos and x²; |·| and cos; |·| and sin). By Theorem 2: continuous

cards.term: Ex 5.1 Q34: find all points of discontinuity of f(x) = |x| − |x + 1|.
cards.definition: A difference of continuous functions: no point of discontinuity (f = 1 for x < −1, −2x − 1 for −1 ≤ x < 0, −1 for x ≥ 0)

cards.term: Trap: is a function continuous if lim x→c f(x) exists?
cards.definition: Not necessarily: the limit must also equal f(c). Example: f(x) = 1 (x ≠ 0), f(0) = 2 has a limit at 0 but is discontinuous there

cards.term: Trap: does a formula like f(x) = (x² − 1)/(x − 1) have a discontinuity at 1?
cards.definition: It is undefined at 1: a removable discontinuity. Defining f(1) = 2 makes it continuous (it equals x + 1 elsewhere)

cards.term: Definition of the derivative of f at c.
cards.definition: f′(c) = lim h→0 [f(c + h) − f(c)]/h, when the limit exists (the slope of the tangent at c)

cards.term: When is f differentiable at c? What are LHD and RHD?
cards.definition: When the left derivative (LHD) lim h→0⁻ [f(c + h) − f(c)]/h equals the right derivative (RHD) lim h→0⁺ [...]/h and both are finite

cards.term: Corners and vertical tangents are where derivatives fail
cards.definition: Differentiable at c iff left derivative = right derivative (finite): corner (|x-1| at 1) and vertical tangent (cube root at 0) are not differentiable though continuous

cards.term: Differentiable implies continuous (not conversely)
cards.definition: If f is differentiable at c then f is continuous at c (Theorem 3); converse false, e.g. |x| at 0; discontinuous implies not differentiable

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Theorem 3

How are “differentiable at c” and “continuous at c” related? Give an example that separates them.

Which set sits inside which?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Theorem 3

How are “differentiable at c” and “continuous at c” related? Give an example that separates them.

Differentiable ⇒ continuous. If f′(c) exists then f(x) − f(c) = [(f(x) − f(c))/(x − c)]·(x − c) → f′(c)·0 = 0, so f(x) → f(c).

The converse is false: f(x) = |x| is continuous at 0 but has a corner there, so it is not differentiable. Hence: not continuous ⇒ not differentiable.

cards.term: Trap: “f is continuous at c, so f′(c) exists”?
cards.definition: False. |x| at 0 and ∛x at 0 are continuous but not differentiable. Only the reverse holds (differentiable ⇒ continuous)

cards.term: Ex 5.2 Q9: show f(x) = |x − 1| is not differentiable at x = 1.
cards.definition: LHD = lim h→0⁻ (|h| − 0)/h = −1; RHD = lim h→0⁺ |h|/h = +1. LHD ≠ RHD

cards.term: Ex 5.2 Q10: show [x] is not differentiable at x = 1 and x = 2.
cards.definition: [x] is not even continuous at integers (left limit c − 1, right limit c), so it cannot be differentiable there. Not differentiable

cards.term: Chain rule: if y = f(u) and u = g(x), dy/dx = ?
cards.definition: dy/dx = (dy/du)·(du/dx) (differentiate the outside, then multiply by the derivative of the inside). For several layers multiply all links

cards.term: Example 21: differentiate sin(x²).
cards.definition: Let t = x²: d/dx sin t = cos t · 2x = 2x cos x²

cards.term: Standard derivatives to know (list).
cards.definition: d/dx: xⁿ → nxⁿ⁻¹; sin x → cos x; cos x → −sin x; tan x → sec²x; cot x → −cosec²x; sec x → sec x tan x; cosec x → −cosec x cot x; eˣ → eˣ; log x → 1/x; aˣ → aˣ log a

cards.term: Standard derivatives of inverse trig functions.
cards.definition: sin⁻¹x → 1/√(1 − x²), cos⁻¹x → −1/√(1 − x²), tan⁻¹x → 1/(1 + x²), cot⁻¹x → −1/(1 + x²), sec⁻¹x → 1/(|x|√(x² − 1)), cosec⁻¹x → −1/(|x|√(x² − 1))

cards.term: Ex 5.2 Q1: differentiate sin(x² + 5).
cards.definition: Chain rule: 2x cos(x² + 5)

cards.term: Ex 5.2 Q2: differentiate cos(sin x).
cards.definition: Outer: −sin(sin x); inner: cos x. −cos x · sin(sin x)

cards.term: Ex 5.2 Q3: differentiate sin(ax + b).
cards.definition: a cos(ax + b)

cards.term: Ex 5.2 Q4: differentiate sec(tan(√x)).
cards.definition: sec(u) tan(u) · du/dx with u = tan √x and du/dx = sec²√x/(2√x): sec(tan√x) · tan(tan√x) · sec²√x / (2√x)

cards.term: Ex 5.2 Q5: differentiate sin(ax + b)/cos(cx + d).
cards.definition: Quotient rule: a cos(ax + b) sec(cx + d) + c sin(ax + b) tan(cx + d) sec(cx + d)

cards.term: Ex 5.2 Q6: differentiate cos x³ · sin²(x⁵).
cards.definition: Product rule: −3x² sin x³ · sin²x⁵ + 10x⁴ sin x⁵ cos x⁵ · cos x³

cards.term: Ex 5.2 Q7: differentiate 2√(cot x²).
cards.definition: y = 2(cot x²)^½, y′ = (cot x²)^(−½)(−cosec²x²)(2x): −2√2 x / (sin x² √(sin 2x²))

cards.term: Ex 5.2 Q8: differentiate cos(√x).
cards.definition: −sin√x/(2√x)

cards.term: Implicit differentiation: method.
cards.definition:
Differentiate both sides with respect to x, treating y as a function of x (so d/dx yⁿ = n yⁿ⁻¹ · dy/dx and d/dx sin y = cos y · dy/dx).
Collect the dy/dx terms and solve

cards.term: Example 23: find dy/dx if y + sin y = cos x.
cards.definition: dy/dx + cos y · dy/dx = −sin x → dy/dx = −sin x/(1 + cos y), y ≠ (2n + 1)π

cards.term: Ex 5.3 Q1: 2x + 3y = sin x.
cards.definition: 2 + 3y′ = cos x → y′ = (cos x − 2)/3

cards.term: Ex 5.3 Q2: 2x + 3y = sin y.
cards.definition: 2 + 3y′ = y′ cos y → y′ = 2/(cos y − 3)

cards.term: Ex 5.3 Q3: ax + by² = cos y.
cards.definition: a + 2by · y′ = −sin y · y′ → y′ = −a/(2by + sin y)

cards.term: Ex 5.3 Q4: xy + y² = tan x + y.
cards.definition: y + xy′ + 2yy′ = sec²x + y′ → y′ = (sec²x − y)/(x + 2y − 1)

cards.term: Ex 5.3 Q5: x² + xy + y² = 100.
cards.definition: 2x + y + xy′ + 2yy′ = 0 → y′ = −(2x + y)/(x + 2y)

cards.term: Ex 5.3 Q6: x³ + x²y + xy² + y³ = 81.
cards.definition: 3x² + 2xy + x²y′ + y² + 2xyy′ + 3y²y′ = 0 → y′ = −(3x² + 2xy + y²)/(x² + 2xy + 3y²)

cards.term: Ex 5.3 Q7: sin²y + cos xy = κ.
cards.definition: 2 sin y cos y · y′ − sin(xy)(y + xy′) = 0 → y′ = y sin xy / (sin 2y − x sin xy)

cards.term: Ex 5.3 Q8: sin²x + cos²y = 1.
cards.definition: 2 sin x cos x − 2 cos y sin y · y′ = 0 → y′ = sin 2x/sin 2y

cards.term: Method: differentiating inverse trig expressions like sin⁻¹(2x/(1 + x²)).
cards.definition:
Simplify first by a substitution (x = tan θ, sin θ, cos θ, …) to a multiple of one inverse function, then differentiate.
This turns a heavy chain rule into a one-line answer (Ex 5.3 Q9–Q15)

cards.term: Ex 5.3 Q9: y = sin⁻¹(2x/(1 + x²)).
cards.definition: x = tan θ: y = sin⁻¹(sin 2θ) = 2 tan⁻¹x (valid for |x| ≤ 1). dy/dx = 2/(1 + x²)
x = tan θ: y = tan⁻¹(tan 3θ) = 3 tan⁻¹x. dy/dx = 3/(1 + x²)
x = tan θ: y = cos⁻¹(cos 2θ) = 2θ. dy/dx = 2/(1 + x²)
x = tan θ: (1 − x²)/(1 + x²) = cos 2θ, y = sin⁻¹(cos 2θ) = π/2 − 2θ. dy/dx = −2/(1 + x²)
x = tan θ: y = cos⁻¹(sin 2θ) = π/2 − 2θ. dy/dx = −2/(1 + x²)
x = sin θ: y = sin⁻¹(sin 2θ) = 2θ. dy/dx = 2/√(1 − x²)
sec⁻¹(1/u) = cos⁻¹u, so y = cos⁻¹(2x² − 1) = 2 cos⁻¹x (x = cos θ). dy/dx = −2/√(1 − x²)

cards.term: Example 24: derivative of sin⁻¹x?
cards.definition: y = sin⁻¹x → x = sin y → 1 = cos y · y′ → y′ = 1/cos y = 1/√(1 − x²) (cos y ≥ 0 on the principal branch)

cards.term: The exponential function equals its own derivative
cards.definition: d/dx e^x = e^x: the slope of y = e^x at any point equals its height; e^x is its own derivative; d/dx a^x = a^x log a

cards.term: Derivative of aˣ (a > 0)?
cards.definition: aˣ log a. Since aˣ = e^(x log a), the chain rule gives e^(x log a) · log a. For a = e this is eˣ

cards.term: Derivative of log x, and of logₐ x?
cards.definition: d/dx log x = 1/x (x > 0). d/dx logₐ x = 1/(x log a). Also d/dx log|x| = 1/x for x ≠ 0

cards.term: Relation between eˣ and log x?
cards.definition: Inverses: e^(log x) = x for x > 0 and log(eˣ) = x for all real x. Example 25: x = e^(log x) is true only for x > 0

cards.term: Properties of log?
cards.definition: log(ab) = log a + log b; log(a/b) = log a − log b; log(aᵇ) = b log a; log 1 = 0; logₐ b = log b/log a

cards.term: Example 26: differentiate cos⁻¹(eˣ) and e^(cos x).
cards.definition: d/dx cos⁻¹(eˣ) = −eˣ/√(1 − e²ˣ). d/dx e^(cos x) = e^(cos x) · (−sin x) = −(sin x) e^(cos x)

cards.term: Ex 5.4 Q1: differentiate eˣ/sin x.
cards.definition: Quotient rule: eˣ (sin x − cos x)/sin²x

cards.term: Ex 5.4 Q2: differentiate e^(sin⁻¹x).
cards.definition: e^(sin⁻¹x)/√(1 − x²)

cards.term: Ex 5.4 Q3: differentiate e^(x³).
cards.definition: 3x² e^(x³)

cards.term: Ex 5.4 Q4: differentiate sin(tan⁻¹ e^(−x)).
cards.definition: cos(tan⁻¹e^(−x)) · 1/(1 + e^(−2x)) · (−e^(−x)): −e^(−x) cos(tan⁻¹ e^(−x))/(1 + e^(−2x))

cards.term: Ex 5.4 Q5: differentiate log(cos eˣ).
cards.definition: (1/cos eˣ)(−sin eˣ)(eˣ) = −eˣ tan eˣ

cards.term: Ex 5.4 Q6: differentiate eˣ + e^(x²) + ... + e^(x⁵).
cards.definition: Term by term: eˣ + 2x e^(x²) + 3x² e^(x³) + 4x³ e^(x⁴) + 5x⁴ e^(x⁵)

cards.term: Ex 5.4 Q7: differentiate √(e^√x), x > 0.
Ex 5.4 Q8: differentiate log(log x), x > 1.
cards.definition: (1/log x) · (1/x) = 1/(x log x)

cards.term: Ex 5.4 Q9: differentiate cos x/log x, x > 0.
cards.definition: Quotient rule: −(x sin x log x + cos x)/(x (log x)²)

cards.term: Ex 5.4 Q10: differentiate cos(log x + eˣ), x > 0.
cards.definition: −sin(log x + eˣ) · (1/x + eˣ)

cards.term: When do you use logarithmic differentiation?
cards.definition: For y = u(x)^v(x) (variable base and exponent) and for long products/quotients/roots. Take log, differentiate: (1/y) y′ = v′ log u + v u′/u, so y′ = y [v′ log u + v u′/u]

cards.term: Why must u(x) > 0 in log differentiation?
cards.definition: Because log u is defined only for positive u. For a product of many factors the sign does not matter for the final algebra, but the method needs u > 0

cards.term: Example 29: differentiate x^(sin x), x > 0.
cards.definition: log y = sin x log x → y′/y = cos x log x + sin x/x → y′ = x^(sin x) [ (sin x)/x + cos x log x ]

cards.term: Logarithmic differentiation of xˣ
cards.definition: y = x^x: log y = x log x, y'/y = 1 + log x, y' = x^x (1 + log x)

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Logarithmic differentiation

Find dy/dx for y = xˣ (x > 0).

y = xˣ
  1. Take log: log y = x log x
  2. Differentiate: (1/y) y′ = log x + x · (1/x) = log x + 1
  3. ?
  4. Check at x = 1: y′ = 1 · 1 = 1 (slope of xˣ at x = 1)
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Logarithmic differentiation

Find dy/dx for y = xˣ (x > 0).

y = xˣ
  1. Take log: log y = x log x
  2. Differentiate: (1/y) y′ = log x + x · (1/x) = log x + 1
  3. Multiply by y: y′ = xˣ (1 + log x)
  4. Check at x = 1: y′ = 1 · 1 = 1 (slope of xˣ at x = 1)

cards.term: Ex 5.5 Q1: differentiate cos x · cos 2x · cos 3x.
cards.definition: Log differentiation: y′ = y(−tan x − 2 tan 2x − 3 tan 3x). −cos x cos 2x cos 3x [tan x + 2 tan 2x + 3 tan 3x]

cards.term: Ex 5.5 Q3: differentiate (log x)^(cos x).
cards.definition: log y = cos x · log(log x). y′ = (log x)^(cos x) [cos x/(x log x) − sin x log(log x)]

cards.term: Ex 5.5 Q4: differentiate x^x − 2^(sin x).
cards.definition: d/dx x^x = x^x(1 + log x); d/dx 2^(sin x) = 2^(sin x) log 2 cos x. x^x (1 + log x) − 2^(sin x) cos x log 2

cards.term: Ex 5.5 Q5: differentiate (x + 3)²(x + 4)³(x + 5)⁴.
Ex 5.5 Q6: differentiate (x + 1/x)^x + x^(1 + 1/x).
cards.definition: (x + 1/x)^x [ (x² − 1)/(x² + 1) + log(x + 1/x) ] + x^(1 + 1/x) [ (x + 1 − log x)/x² ]

cards.term: Ex 5.5 Q7: differentiate (log x)^x + x^(log x).
cards.definition: (log x)^(x−1) [1 + log x · log(log x)] + 2 x^(log x − 1) log x

cards.term: Ex 5.5 Q8: differentiate (sin x)^x + sin⁻¹√x.
cards.definition: (sin x)^x [x cot x + log sin x] + 1/(2√(x − x²))

cards.term: Ex 5.5 Q9: differentiate x^(sin x) + (sin x)^(cos x).
cards.definition: x^(sin x)[sin x/x + cos x log x] + (sin x)^(cos x)[cos x cot x − sin x log sin x]

cards.term: Ex 5.5 Q10: differentiate x^(x cos x) + (x² + 1)/(x² − 1).
cards.definition: x^(x cos x)[cos x (1 + log x) − x sin x log x] − 4x/(x² − 1)²

cards.term: Ex 5.5 Q11: differentiate (x cos x)^x + (x sin x)^(1/x).
cards.definition: (x cos x)^x [1 − x tan x + log(x cos x)] + (x sin x)^(1/x) [ (x cot x + 1 − log(x sin x))/x² ]

cards.term: Ex 5.5 Q12: dy/dx if x^y + y^x = 1.
cards.definition: Differentiate x^y and y^x by logs: dy/dx = −(y x^(y−1) + y^x log y)/(x^y log x + x y^(x−1))

cards.term: Ex 5.5 Q13: dy/dx if y^x = x^y.
cards.definition: x log y = y log x → dy/dx = (y/x)(y − x log y)/(x − y log x)

cards.term: Ex 5.5 Q14: dy/dx if (cos x)^y = (cos y)^x.
cards.definition: y log cos x = x log cos y → dy/dx = (y tan x + log cos y)/(x tan y + log cos x)

cards.term: Ex 5.5 Q15: dy/dx if xy = e^(x − y).
cards.definition: log x + log y = x − y → 1/x + y′/y = 1 − y′ → dy/dx = y(x − 1)/(x(y + 1))

cards.term: Ex 5.5 Q17: differentiate (x² − 5x + 8)(x³ + 7x + 9) three ways.
cards.definition: (i) Product rule (ii) expand to x⁵ − 5x⁴ + 15x³ − 26x² + 11x + 72 and differentiate (iii) logarithmic differentiation. All agree: 5x⁴ − 20x³ + 45x² − 52x + 11

cards.term: Ex 5.5 Q18: prove d(uvw)/dx = u′vw + uv′w + uvw′.
cards.definition: Product rule twice: (uv)w gives (uv)′w + uvw′ = (u′v + uv′)w + uvw′. Or log: (uvw)′/(uvw) = u′/u + v′/v + w′/w. ✓

cards.term: Trap: is d/dx (xˣ) = x · x^(x−1) = xˣ?
cards.definition: No. The power rule needs a constant exponent, the exponential rule a constant base. For xˣ use logs: xˣ(1 + log x)

cards.term: Derivative of a parametric curve x = f(t), y = g(t)?
cards.definition: dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt), provided dx/dt ≠ 0. No need to eliminate t

cards.term: Derivative of a parametric curve: dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt)
cards.definition: Parametric: dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt); cycloid x=a(t-sin t), y=a(1-cos t) gives dy/dx = cot(t/2); Ex 5.6 Q6 variant y=a(1+cos t) gives -cot(t/2)

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Parametric derivative · cycloid

A point on a rolling circle traces x = a(θ − sin θ), y = a(1 − cos θ). Find dy/dx.

Differentiate x and y with respect to θ first.

cards.term: Ex 5.6 Q1: x = 2at², y = at⁴.
cards.definition: dx/dt = 4at, dy/dt = 4at³: dy/dx = t²

cards.term: Ex 5.6 Q2: x = a cos θ, y = b cos θ.
cards.definition: dx/dθ = −a sin θ, dy/dθ = −b sin θ: dy/dx = b/a

cards.term: Ex 5.6 Q3: x = sin t, y = cos 2t.
cards.definition: dx/dt = cos t, dy/dt = −2 sin 2t = −4 sin t cos t: dy/dx = −4 sin t
dx/dt = 4, dy/dt = −4/t²: dy/dx = −1/t²

cards.term: Ex 5.6 Q5: x = cos θ − cos 2θ, y = sin θ − sin 2θ.
cards.definition: dx/dθ = −sin θ + 2 sin 2θ, dy/dθ = cos θ − 2 cos 2θ: dy/dx = (cos θ − 2 cos 2θ)/(2 sin 2θ − sin θ)

cards.term: Ex 5.6 Q6: x = a(θ − sin θ), y = a(1 + cos θ).
cards.definition: dx/dθ = a(1 − cos θ), dy/dθ = −a sin θ: dy/dx = −sin θ/(1 − cos θ) = −cot(θ/2)

cards.term: Ex 5.6 Q7: x = sin³t/√(cos 2t), y = cos³t/√(cos 2t).
cards.definition: After differentiating and simplifying: dy/dx = −cot 3t

cards.term: Ex 5.6 Q8: x = a(cos t + log tan(t/2)), y = a sin t.
cards.definition: dx/dt = a(−sin t + 1/sin t) = a cos²t/sin t, dy/dt = a cos t: dy/dx = tan t

cards.term: Ex 5.6 Q9: x = a sec θ, y = b tan θ.
cards.definition: dx/dθ = a sec θ tan θ, dy/dθ = b sec²θ: dy/dx = (b/a) cosec θ

cards.term: Ex 5.6 Q10: x = a(cos θ + θ sin θ), y = a(sin θ − θ cos θ).
cards.definition: dx/dθ = aθ cos θ, dy/dθ = aθ sin θ: dy/dx = tan θ

cards.term: Ex 5.6 Q11: x = √(a^(sin⁻¹t)), y = √(a^(cos⁻¹t)). Show dy/dx = −y/x.
cards.definition: x = a^(½ sin⁻¹t), y = a^(½ cos⁻¹t): dx/dt = x log a/(2√(1 − t²)), dy/dt = −y log a/(2√(1 − t²)). Divide: dy/dx = −y/x ✓ (also xy = a^(π/4), constant)

cards.term: Notation for the second derivative?
cards.definition: d²y/dx² = f″(x) = y″ = y₂: differentiate f′(x) once more. The derivative of the derivative

cards.term: For a parametric curve, is d²y/dx² = (d²y/dt²)/(d²x/dt²)?
cards.definition: No. Differentiate dy/dx (a function of t) with respect to t and divide by dx/dt again: d²y/dx² = [d(dy/dx)/dt]/(dx/dt)

cards.term: Example 36: y = A sin x + B cos x. Show y″ + y = 0.
cards.definition: y′ = A cos x − B sin x; y″ = −A sin x − B cos x = −y. ✓

cards.term: Example 37: y = 3e^(2x) + 2e^(3x). Show y″ − 5y′ + 6y = 0.
Example 38: y = sin⁻¹x. Show (1 − x²) y″ − x y′ = 0.
cards.definition: y′ = 1/√(1 − x²), so √(1 − x²) y′ = 1. Differentiate: √(1 − x²) y″ − x y′/√(1 − x²) = 0. Multiply by √(1 − x²): (1 − x²)y″ − xy′ = 0 ✓

cards.term: Ex 5.7 Q1: y = x² + 3x + 2. Find y″.
cards.definition: y′ = 2x + 3, y″ = 2

cards.term: Ex 5.7 Q2: y = x²⁰. Find y″.
cards.definition: 380 x¹⁸ (20 · 19 = 380)

cards.term: Ex 5.7 Q3: y = x cos x.
cards.definition: y′ = cos x − x sin x; y″ = −x cos x − 2 sin x

cards.term: Ex 5.7 Q4: y = log x.
cards.definition: y′ = 1/x; y″ = −1/x²

cards.term: Ex 5.7 Q5: y = x³ log x.
cards.definition: y′ = 3x² log x + x²; y″ = x(5 + 6 log x)

cards.term: Ex 5.7 Q6: y = eˣ sin 5x.
cards.definition: y′ = eˣ(sin 5x + 5 cos 5x); y″ = 2eˣ(5 cos 5x − 12 sin 5x)

cards.term: Ex 5.7 Q7: y = e^(6x) cos 3x.
cards.definition: y′ = e^(6x)(6 cos 3x − 3 sin 3x); y″ = 9e^(6x)(3 cos 3x − 4 sin 3x)

cards.term: Ex 5.7 Q8: y = tan⁻¹x.
cards.definition: y′ = 1/(1 + x²); y″ = −2x/(1 + x²)²

cards.term: Ex 5.7 Q9: y = log(log x).
cards.definition: y′ = 1/(x log x); y″ = −(1 + log x)/(x log x)²

cards.term: Ex 5.7 Q10: y = sin(log x).
cards.definition: y′ = cos(log x)/x; y″ = −[sin(log x) + cos(log x)]/x²

cards.term: Ex 5.7 Q11: y = 5 cos x − 3 sin x. Prove y″ + y = 0.
cards.definition: y′ = −5 sin x − 3 cos x, y″ = −5 cos x + 3 sin x = −y. ✓

cards.term: Ex 5.7 Q12: y = cos⁻¹x. Find d²y/dx² in terms of y alone.
cards.definition: y′ = −1/√(1 − x²) and y″ = −x/(1 − x²)^(3/2). With x = cos y, √(1 − x²) = sin y: y″ = −cot y cosec²y

cards.term: Ex 5.7 Q13: y = 3 cos(log x) + 4 sin(log x). Show x²y₂ + xy₁ + y = 0.
cards.definition: xy₁ = −3 sin(log x) + 4 cos(log x); differentiate: x y₂ + y₁ = −3 cos(log x)/x − 4 sin(log x)/x = −y/x. Multiply by x: x²y₂ + xy₁ + y = 0 ✓

cards.term: Ex 5.7 Q14: y = Ae^(mx) + Be^(nx). Show y″ − (m + n)y′ + mny = 0.
cards.definition: The coefficient of Ae^(mx) is m² − (m + n)m + mn = 0 and of Be^(nx) is n² − (m + n)n + mn = 0. ✓

cards.term: Ex 5.7 Q16: eʸ(x + 1) = 1. Show y″ = (y′)².
cards.definition: y = −log(x + 1), y′ = −1/(x + 1), y″ = 1/(x + 1)² = (y′)². ✓

cards.term: Ex 5.7 Q17: y = (tan⁻¹x)². Show (x² + 1)²y₂ + 2x(x² + 1)y₁ = 2.
cards.definition: y₁ = 2 tan⁻¹x/(1 + x²), so (1 + x²)y₁ = 2 tan⁻¹x. Differentiate: (1 + x²)y₂ + 2xy₁ = 2/(1 + x²). Multiply by (1 + x²): ✓

cards.term: Example 39(i): differentiate √(3x + 2) + 1/√(2x² + 4).
Example 43: differentiate sin²x with respect to e^(cos x).
cards.definition: du/dv = (du/dx)/(dv/dx) = 2 sin x cos x/(−sin x e^(cos x)) = −2 cos x/e^(cos x). Differentiating one function with respect to another: divide their derivatives

cards.term: Misc Q1: differentiate (3x² − 9x + 5)⁹.
cards.definition: Chain rule: 27(3x² − 9x + 5)⁸ (2x − 3)

cards.term: Misc Q2: differentiate sin³x + cos⁶x.
cards.definition: 3 sin²x cos x − 6 cos⁵x sin x = 3 sin x cos x (sin x − 2 cos⁴x)

cards.term: Misc Q3: differentiate (5x)^(3cos 2x).
cards.definition: log y = 3 cos 2x log 5x: (5x)^(3cos 2x) [3 cos 2x/x − 6 sin 2x log 5x]

cards.term: Misc Q4: differentiate sin⁻¹(x√x), 0 ≤ x ≤ 1.
Misc Q5: differentiate cos⁻¹(x/2)/√(2x + 7), −2 < x < 2.
Misc Q6: differentiate cot⁻¹[(√(1 + sin x) + √(1 − sin x))/(√(1 + sin x) − √(1 − sin x))], 0 < x < π/2.
cards.definition: The fraction equals cot(x/2) (as in the inverse trig chapter), so y = x/2. dy/dx = 1/2

cards.term: Misc Q7: differentiate (log x)^(log x), x > 1.
cards.definition: (log x)^(log x) [1/x + log(log x)/x]

cards.term: Misc Q8: differentiate cos(a cos x + b sin x).
cards.definition: (a sin x − b cos x) sin(a cos x + b sin x)

cards.term: Misc Q9: differentiate (sin x − cos x)^(sin x − cos x), π/4 < x < 3π/4.
cards.definition: Base u = sin x − cos x > 0: y = u^u, y′ = u^u (1 + log u) u′ with u′ = cos x + sin x. (sin x − cos x)^(sin x − cos x) (cos x + sin x)(1 + log(sin x − cos x))

cards.term: Misc Q10: differentiate x^x + x^a + a^x + a^a (a > 0 fixed).
cards.definition: x^x (1 + log x) + a x^(a−1) + a^x log a (a^a is a constant, derivative 0)

cards.term: Misc Q11: differentiate x^(x² − 3) + (x − 3)^(x²), x > 3.
cards.definition: x^(x²−3)[(x² − 3)/x + 2x log x] + (x − 3)^(x²)[x²/(x − 3) + 2x log(x − 3)]

cards.term: Misc Q12: dy/dx if y = 12(1 − cos t), x = 10(t − sin t), −π/2 < t < π/2.
cards.definition: dy/dt = 12 sin t, dx/dt = 10(1 − cos t): dy/dx = (6/5) sin t/(1 − cos t) = (6/5) cot(t/2)

cards.term: Misc Q13: dy/dx if y = sin⁻¹x + sin⁻¹√(1 − x²), 0 < x < 1.
cards.definition: With x = sin θ (0 < θ < π/2): sin⁻¹√(1 − x²) = cos⁻¹x... y = θ + (π/2 − θ) = π/2, a constant. dy/dx = 0

cards.term: Misc Q14: if x√(1 + y) + y√(1 + x) = 0, −1 < x < 1, prove dy/dx = −1/(1 + x)².
cards.definition: Then y = −x/(1 + x) (solve: x²(1 + y) = y²(1 + x) → (x − y)(x + y + xy) = 0). So y′ = −1/(1 + x)². ✓

cards.term: Misc Q15: (x − a)² + (y − b)² = c². Show [1 + (y′)²]^(3/2)/y″ is a constant independent of a and b.
cards.definition: With u = x − a, v = y − b: y′ = −u/v, y″ = −(u² + v²)/v³ = −c²/v³, and 1 + y′² = c²/v². The ratio is ±c (constant), its sign depending only on whether y > b or y < b

cards.term: Misc Q16: cos y = x cos(a + y), cos a ≠ ±1. Prove dy/dx = cos²(a + y)/sin a.
cards.definition: x = cos y/cos(a + y). Differentiate: dx/dy = sin a/cos²(a + y). Invert: dy/dx = cos²(a + y)/sin a ✓

cards.term: Misc Q17: x = a(cos t + t sin t), y = a(sin t − t cos t). Find d²y/dx².
cards.definition: dy/dx = tan t (Ex 5.6 Q10). Then d²y/dx² = sec²t/(dx/dt) = sec²t/(at cos t) = sec³t/(at), 0 < t < π/2

cards.term: Misc Q18: f(x) = |x|³. Show f″(x) exists for all real x and find it.
cards.definition: f = x³ (x ≥ 0), −x³ (x < 0): f′ = 3x², −3x²; f″ = 6x, −6x, and both are 0 at x = 0: f″(x) = 6|x|

cards.term: Misc Q19: use sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B and differentiation to obtain cos(A + B).
cards.definition: Differentiate with respect to A (B fixed): cos(A + B) = cos A cos B − sin A sin B. ✓ (or with respect to B)

cards.term: Misc Q20: is there a function continuous everywhere but not differentiable at exactly two points?
cards.definition: Yes: f(x) = |x| + |x − 1| has corners at x = 0 and x = 1 and is smooth elsewhere

cards.term: Misc Q21: y = |f g h; l m n; a b c| (a determinant). Prove dy/dx = |f′ g′ h′; l m n; a b c|.
cards.definition: Only the first row contains functions of x; the other entries are constants. Differentiating the determinant expansion row 1 gives the same determinant with row 1 replaced by the derivatives. ✓

cards.term: Misc Q22: y = e^(a cos⁻¹x), −1 ≤ x ≤ 1. Show (1 − x²)y″ − xy′ − a²y = 0.
cards.definition: y′ = −a y/√(1 − x²), so (1 − x²)y′² = a²y². Differentiate to get (1 − x²)y″ − xy′ − a²y = 0. ✓

cards.term: Number of points where f(x) = |x − 1| + |x − 2| + |x − 3| is not differentiable?
cards.definition: Corners at x = 1, 2, 3: three points (each modulus has a corner)

cards.term: f(x) = |sin x| is not differentiable at which points?
cards.definition: x = nπ (n ∈ Z): the graph has a corner where sin x crosses zero

cards.term: Is f(x) = x|x| differentiable at 0? Twice differentiable?
cards.definition: f = x² (x ≥ 0), −x² (x < 0). f′ = 2|x|, so yes at 0 with f′(0) = 0. But f′ = 2|x| has a corner at 0, so f″(0) does not exist

cards.term: Find f′(0) for f(x) = x² sin(1/x) (x ≠ 0), f(0) = 0.
cards.definition: From the definition: (h² sin(1/h))/h = h sin(1/h) → 0. But f′(x) = 2x sin(1/x) − cos(1/x) is not continuous at 0

cards.term: Continuity vs differentiability of f(x) = x sin(1/x) (x ≠ 0), f(0) = 0?
cards.definition: Continuous at 0 (|x sin(1/x)| ≤ |x|) but not differentiable at 0 (the difference quotient sin(1/h) oscillates)

cards.term: For what value of k is f(x) = (sin 3x)/x (x ≠ 0), k (x = 0) continuous at 0?
cards.definition: lim x→0 sin 3x/x = 3. k = 3

cards.term: Find a, b if f(x) = ax + b (x ≥ 1), x² (x < 1)... is continuous and differentiable at 1.
cards.definition: Continuity: a + b = 1. Differentiability: a = 2 (derivative of x² at 1). So a = 2, b = −1

cards.term: Chain rule for three layers: differentiate sin(cos(tan x)).
cards.definition: Outside to inside: cos(cos(tan x)) · (−sin(tan x)) · sec²x = −cos(cos tan x) sin(tan x) sec²x

cards.term: d/dx of |x| for x ≠ 0?
cards.definition: |x|/x (= 1 for x > 0, −1 for x < 0). Undefined at 0. Also d/dx |f(x)| = f f′/|f|

cards.term: If f(x) = x² + 3x + 1... find d/dx f(f(x)) at x = 0.
cards.definition: f′(x) = 2x + 3; f(0) = 1; chain rule: f′(f(0)) f′(0) = f′(1) f′(0) = 5 × 3 = 15

cards.term: If y = x^(x^x), find dy/dx at x = 1.
cards.definition: log y = x^x log x. At x = 1: y = 1, x^x = 1. d/dx(x^x log x) = x^x(1 + log x) log x + x^x/x = (1)(1)(0) + 1 = 1. So y′/y = 1 and dy/dx = 1

cards.term: Differentiate y = x^(1/x) (x > 0).
cards.definition: log y = (log x)/x: y′/y = (1 − log x)/x². y′ = x^(1/x)(1 − log x)/x² (zero at x = e: the maximum)

cards.term: Logarithmic derivative of a product f = f₁f₂···fₙ?
cards.definition: f′ = f · Σ fᵢ′/fᵢ. Handy for Ex 5.5 Q1, Q2 and Q16

cards.term:
MCQ: the function f(x) = |x − 2| is
(a) not continuous at 2 (b) continuous but not differentiable at 2 (c) differentiable at 2 (d) not defined at 2
cards.definition: Continuous with a corner: (b)

cards.term:
MCQ: f(x) = [x] is discontinuous at
(a) integers only (b) rationals only (c) no point (d) all real numbers
cards.definition: (a) integers only

cards.term:
MCQ: if f(x) = (x² − 4)/(x − 2) (x ≠ 2) is continuous at x = 2, then f(2) =
(a) 0 (b) 2 (c) 4 (d) not possible
cards.definition: The limit is 4: (c) 4

cards.term:
MCQ: d/dx (sin⁻¹x + cos⁻¹x) =
(a) 0 (b) 1 (c) π/2 (d) 2/√(1 − x²)
cards.definition: The sum is the constant π/2: (a) 0

cards.term:
MCQ: d/dx (xˣ) at x = 1 is
(a) 0 (b) 1 (c) e (d) 2
cards.definition: xˣ(1 + log x) at 1 = 1: (b) 1

cards.term:
MCQ: d/dx (log₁₀ x) =
(a) 1/x (b) 1/(x log 10) (c) log 10/x (d) x/log 10
cards.definition: (b)

cards.term:
MCQ: if y = e^(2x), then d²y/dx² at x = 0 is
(a) 1 (b) 2 (c) 4 (d) 8
cards.definition: y″ = 4e^(2x) = 4: (c) 4

cards.term:
MCQ: if x = t², y = t³ then dy/dx =
(a) 3t/2 (b) 2t/3 (c) t (d) 3t²
cards.definition: (3t²)/(2t): (a) 3t/2

cards.term:
MCQ: the derivative of sin x with respect to cos x is
(a) −cot x (b) tan x (c) cot x (d) −tan x
cards.definition: cos x/(−sin x): (a) −cot x

cards.term:
MCQ: if f(x) = x + 5 (x ≤ 1), kx + 3 (x > 1) is continuous, k =
(a) 1 (b) 3 (c) 6 (d) 0
cards.definition: 6 = k + 3: (b) 3

cards.term: Integer answer (JEE Main): the number of points where f(x) = |x² − 4| is not differentiable is?
cards.definition: Corners where x² − 4 changes sign: 2 (x = ±2)

cards.term: Integer answer: if f(x) = x³ − 3x, the value of f′(2) is?
cards.definition: 3x² − 3 = 12 − 3 = 9

cards.term: Integer answer: if y = x^(2x), the value of dy/dx at x = 1 is?
cards.definition: log y = 2x log x, y′/y = 2 log x + 2. At x = 1: y = 1, so dy/dx = 2

cards.term:
Assertion–Reason.
A: f(x) = |x| is continuous at 0 but not differentiable at 0.
R: the left and right derivatives of |x| at 0 are −1 and +1.
(a) Both true, R explains A (b) Both true, R does not (c) A true, R false (d) A false, R true
cards.definition: (a)

cards.term:
Assertion–Reason.
A: if f is differentiable at c, it is continuous at c.
R: if f is continuous at c then it is differentiable at c.
(a) Both true, R explains A (b) Both true, R does not (c) A true, R false (d) A false, R true
cards.definition: (c): R is the false converse

cards.term: True/False: the derivative of a constant is 1.
cards.definition: False: it is 0

cards.term: True/False: every polynomial is differentiable everywhere.
cards.definition: True

cards.term: 2-mark: find dy/dx if y = sin(x²).
cards.definition: 2x cos x²

cards.term: 2-mark: examine the continuity of f(x) = 2x + 3 at x = 1.
cards.definition: lim x→1 (2x + 3) = 5 = f(1): continuous

cards.term: 3-mark: if y = x^(sin x), find dy/dx.
cards.definition: log y = sin x log x → dy/dx = x^(sin x)[sin x/x + cos x log x]

cards.term: 3-mark: find dy/dx if x = a cos θ, y = a sin θ.
cards.definition: (a cos θ)/(−a sin θ) = −cot θ

cards.term: 3-mark: if y = e^(sin⁻¹x), show (1 − x²) y″ − x y′ − y = 0.
cards.definition: y′ = y/√(1 − x²), so (1 − x²)y′² = y². Differentiate: (1 − x²)y″ − xy′ − y = 0 after dividing by 2y′. ✓

cards.term: 4-mark: for what value of k is f(x) = kx + 1 (x ≤ π), cos x (x > π) continuous at x = π?
cards.definition: kπ + 1 = −1 → k = −2/π

cards.term: 4-mark: if x = a(t + sin t), y = a(1 − cos t), find dy/dx at t = π/2.
cards.definition: dy/dx = sin t/(1 + cos t) = tan(t/2). At t = π/2: 1

cards.term: 4-mark: differentiate y = (x)^(x) + (sin x)^(x) with respect to x.
cards.definition: xˣ(1 + log x) + (sin x)ˣ(log sin x + x cot x)

cards.term: Case-based: a particle moves so that s = t³ − 6t² + 9t (metres, seconds). Find the velocity and acceleration at t = 2.
cards.definition: v = ds/dt = 3t² − 12t + 9 = −3 m/s at t = 2; a = dv/dt = 6t − 12 = 0 m/s²

cards.term: Case-based: the radius of a circle grows as r = 2t cm. How fast is the area changing at t = 3?
cards.definition: A = πr² = 4πt²; dA/dt = 8πt = 24π cm²/s at t = 3 (chain rule: dA/dt = 2πr dr/dt)
